skill.name: azure-messaging-webpubsub-java
skill.description: Provides Java patterns for Azure Web PubSub clients, targeted messaging, connection management, access tokens, permissions, asynchronous operations, and error handling.

skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 37 external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences or inline role names. The two URL findings are placeholder Azure endpoints, not outbound requests. The review found token URL logging and unscoped group roles in examples.

remediation.issue: The access-token example prints a token-derived URL to standard output.
remediation.suggestion: Remove token URL logging. Log only non-secret metadata, and redact authentication values from application logs and error reports.

remediation.issue: The access-token example grants roles that apply to every group.
remediation.suggestion: Use group-scoped role names, short expiration periods, and server-side authorization before granting token permissions.

semantic_findings.title: Client Access Token URL Logged
semantic_findings.description: The token example prints token.getUrl() to standard output. A client access URL can carry bearer credentials, so application logs may expose Web PubSub access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example directly prints the URL returned for a newly generated client access token. Token-bearing URLs are authentication material and should not enter logs.

semantic_findings.title: Unscoped Group Roles Granted
semantic_findings.description: The token example grants join and send roles without a group suffix. The role table states that these roles apply to any group.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example and role table explicitly show unscoped permissions and their any-group effect. The skill also documents group-scoped alternatives.

content.user_title: Build Azure Web PubSub Apps with Java
content.value_statement: Real-time Java applications need secure, targeted messaging across WebSocket clients. This skill provides Azure Web PubSub patterns for clients, groups, tokens, permissions, async operations, and errors.
actual_capabilities: Creates synchronous or asynchronous Azure Web PubSub clients using connection strings, access keys, or DefaultAzureCredential.
Shows how to send text or JSON messages to all connections, groups, users, or individual connections.
Explains group membership, connection checks, connection closure, and user presence operations.
Demonstrates client access token creation with user identities, roles, groups, and expiration settings.
Covers permission grants, revocation, checks, response filters, and basic HTTP error handling.
limitations: Provides examples and guidance only; it does not deploy Azure resources or run Java applications.
Requires an existing Azure Web PubSub resource, valid credentials, and application-specific authorization decisions.
Does not cover service provisioning, event handlers, client-side WebSocket code, monitoring, or production testing.
SDK versions and Azure behavior may change, so verify generated code against current Microsoft documentation.

use_cases.title: Add targeted application updates
use_cases.description: Create Java service code that sends authorized notifications to selected users, connections, or groups.

use_cases.title: Standardize messaging integration
use_cases.description: Define consistent client creation, authentication, async handling, and connection management patterns across services.

use_cases.title: Review token permissions
use_cases.description: Evaluate access token roles, expiration, group scope, and permission grants before production release.

prompt_templates.title: Create a service client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create an Azure Web PubSub Java service client with DefaultAzureCredential for hub {hub_name}.

prompt_templates.title: Send group updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Java code that sends {message_type} updates to group {group_name}. Include error handling and explain each required SDK type.

prompt_templates.title: Issue a scoped token
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short-lived token for user {user_id} that can only send to group {group_name}. Avoid broad roles and secret logging.

prompt_templates.title: Review a production design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Azure Web PubSub Java design: {design}. Identify authorization, token handling, filtering, async, and connection lifecycle risks. Propose safer patterns.

output_examples.input: Send release updates to premium users without broadcasting to every connection.
output_examples.output: Recommended approach: place authorized connections in a premium-users group, send updates to that group, and handle service errors explicitly.

output_examples.input: Create browser access for one user who can send messages only to the support group.
output_examples.output: Use a short-lived token with the authenticated user identity and a support-group send role. Never print the token URL.

output_examples.input: Explain how an asynchronous group send should report success and failure.
output_examples.output: Subscribe to the async result, record a non-secret success event, and route failures through structured error handling.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential when possible, and keep connection strings or access keys outside source control.
Grant group-scoped roles with short token lifetimes and authenticated user identities.
Validate recipients, handle HTTP failures, and test disconnect behavior before production deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not print token URLs, connection strings, access keys, or full authentication errors.
Do not grant unscoped send or join roles when one group is sufficient.
Do not broadcast user-controlled content without authorization, validation, and rate controls.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Java service clients, message delivery, groups, connections, client tokens, permissions, async operations, and basic error handling.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. You need an existing Azure Web PubSub resource and valid credentials.

faq.question: Which authentication methods are shown?
faq.answer: The examples include connection strings, AzureKeyCredential, and DefaultAzureCredential.

faq.question: Does it support synchronous and asynchronous clients?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents both client types and shows asynchronous success and error callbacks.

faq.question: Can it help create client access tokens?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains user identities, roles, initial groups, and expiration settings. Treat every generated token as a secret.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Validate authorization, secret handling, retry behavior, observability, SDK versions, and load characteristics for your environment.
